limitations: Order 12 itself stays open: 51 non-quasigroup CNFs were undecided after 1,000,000 conflicts each, and the hardest survived further probes (with a missing-value split and with implied 'star' clauses). A model of order 12 would be the smallest non-right-cancellative model of 677 known.
novelty_basis: No complete or quasigroup-only search of 677 at order 12 is reported in the sources read (reviews/historian_677_nonqg.md, Q4): anti-255 searches at order 12 never terminated (J. Hyun, Oct 30, 2025) and restricted searches covered other classes; the eq677 database has no model of order 12 and calls orders 12 and 14 open. The smallest known non-right-cancellative model has order 25 (M. Reinke, Nov 26, 2025).
proof_check: computer-assisted - the 138 cases refuted by EXP-C05-11 and, for the other 57 cases of Lemma 8, the quasigroup parts (Latin columns and the column division clauses of Lemma 9') and 6 non-quasigroup parts refuted by EXP-C05-13, every refutation a DRAT proof from CaDiCaL 1.5.3 verified by drat-trim; the split by right cancellation is exhaustive (systems.magma_split.build, tested); upheld by the independent Skeptic (reviews/skeptic_batch1.2.md, section 10: counts and hashes checked, three quasigroup parts re-decided with an independent encoder and Glucose 4, proofs verified)
statement: No quasigroup of order 12 satisfies law 677, x = y(x((yx)y)): every finite model of order 12, if one exists, is not right-cancellative. Moreover 677 has a model of order 12 iff one of the 51 non-quasigroup part CNFs listed in results/EXP-C05-13.json is satisfiable; so such a model is either idempotent with a row having exactly one fixed point, or has a non-idempotent element a with the fewest fixed points whose row has at most one fixed point and moves a in a cycle of length at least 4.
title: Law 677 has no quasigroup model of order 12; a model of order 12 exists iff one of 51 explicit non-quasigroup case CNFs is satisfiable
